text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

E.W. Cox, a subsidiary of Hong Kong-based construction and building services company Wah Tung International Holdings Ltd, has acquired a A$3.1 million tender to replace the Sydney Harbour Bridge's four historic arch cranes - a move which will be the 64-yer-old bridge's first upgrade. Page 2.

Energy Resources of Australia's proposed Jabiluka uranium mine received a setback yesterday when the traditional Aboriginal owners rejected the company's draft environmental impact statement. The mine needs the consent of Aboriginal traditional owners beore it can proceed. Page 3.

In a proposed test case before the Australian Industrial Relations Commission, the ACTU is seeking to amend federal award clauses aimed at improving minimum redundancy pay entitlements and to make employers consult more with employees over changes to job levels. Page 5.

In a joint venture, the Melbourne-based Linfox transport group and British aviation contract specialists Serco are to buy the Avalon airport near Geelong from the federal government. Finance Minister John Fahey said the sale would profit the Government by A$11 million in net present value. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Reserve Bank has adopted a stance in conflict with Treasury by supporting plans to limit the federal government's protection of bank deposits. The Reserve argues that the existing legal obligations of the central bank are unclear and unsound, whereas the Treasury favours the introduction of a commercially based deposit insurance protection scheme. Page 1.

Safe on dry land again, rescued yachtsmen Tony Bullimore and Thierry Dubois provided new details of their incredible tale of survival, while the unsung heroes of the Royal Australian Navy and Royal Australian Air Force, who were responsible for the rescue, were praised for their efforts. Page 1.

After agreeing to pay A$340 million to take management control of the Sydney Harbour Casino, the Packer family's premier listed company, Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, which owns the Nine Network and Australia's largest magazine group, is expected to pressure the New South Wales Government to lower tax rates for interstate and offshore "high-roller" gamblers. Page 1.

Tropical Public Health Unit medical entomologist Scott Ritchie revealed yesterday the Queensland Government has warned that the state's tropical north is at risk of a record-breaking epidemic of the potentially fatal dengue fever - a mosquito-borne disease. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Speaking at a gathering of thousands of well-wishers, politicians and journalists in Fremantle yesterday, 58-year-old Tony Bullimore, the Briton who survived four days in an upturned yacht hull in freezing Southern Ocean waters, thanked Australia for its generosity and said both he and Thierry Dubois owed their lives to the professionalism and dedication of the Australian Defence Forces. Page 1.

Opening the Crown case in a committal hearing of charges against Sydney identity Bill Bayeh, his wife, Tanya, Peter Kay, his wife, Roula, Dominic Pedavoli and another man known only as "Mr L", Crown prosecutor John Kiely told magistrate Elwyn Elms yesterday that Bayeh allegedly made a profit of nearly A$500,000 in six months selling cocaine and heroin from the Cosmo Coffee Lounge at Kings Cross. Page 3.

In a five-page letter written shortly after he appeared before the Parliamentary Committee on the Independent Commission Against Corruption last month, the head of the ICAC, Barry O'Keefe, complained about antagonism, bullying and insults from a parliamntary committee that monitors his performance. Page 3.
THE AGE

Police sources have told The Age that an amphetamine dealer paid officers A$100,000 for information obtained during a raid by the drug squad. The files were stolen from the St Kilda Road police complex and a police spokesman James Tonkin said that a secuity review had been ordered there. Page A1.

As part of a plan to increase his interests in the casino and gaming industries, Kerry Packer has offered A$342 million for a 10 percent stake in the Sydney Harbour Casino and a controlling 85 percent stake in its managing company. The head of Melbourne's Crown Casino, Lloyd Williams, reacted positively to the news saying it heralded an alliance between the two operations. Page A1.

Senior Detective Peter Ure, of Ballarat CIB, told Ballarat Magistrates Court yesterday that three people had been arrested while allegedly conducting an exorcism on two children - a three-year-old and a 21-month-old baby. The adults had been found naked beside the Great Western Highway. The mother of the children told police that she feared her children were possessed by demons. Page A1.

A total fire ban has been imposed on Metropolitan Melbourne with the Country Fire Authority and the Department of Natural Resources and Environment battling various bushfires around the state. The CFA's chief officer Trevor Roche said the ban has been imposed in response to high temperatures, strong winds and dropping humidity. Page A3.
